The strongest verified deployment records are Agility's more than 65,000 operating hours across nine customer facilities and Unitree's roughly 5,500 units shipped in 2025; the "no manufacturer has documented more than 1,000 deployed units" status call is the milestone's own editorial framing on top of these records.

RoboArena deliberately crowd-sources double-blind pairwise evaluations across a distributed network of evaluators instead of standardizing fixed tasks, RoboChallenge provides a reproducible online evaluation system, and ManipulationNet delivers reproducible task setups through standardized hardware kits.
RL-100 attains 100 percent success across 1,000 of 1,000 evaluation episodes on eight diverse real-robot tasks; the final pi*0.6 model is in the 90%+ range on all tasks except diverse laundry.

Sparsh-X is trained on roughly one million contact-rich interactions collected with the Digit 360 sensor, and TouchWorld is a predictive-and-reactive tactile foundation model for dexterous manipulation; the "outside every major VLA pipeline" half of the status call is the milestone's own editorial framing, not a source-certified absence.

EgoScale trains a VLA on over 20,854 hours of action-labeled egocentric human video and uncovers a log-linear scaling law between human data scale and validation loss, which correlates with downstream real-robot performance; the R² = 0.9983 constant in the statusDetail is not re-verified by this pass (the retained base holds the abs page only).

evidence.supportingPassage: For quantitative comparisons, we use a set of mock home environments to provide a controlled and reproducible setup, while the most realistic final evaluation is conducted in three real homes that were not part of the training set (see Figure 6).

Agility Robotics has the broader commercial footprint. The company says its Digit robot has accumulated more than 65,000 operating hours across nine customer facilities, naming GXO, Schaeffler, Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada and Mercado Libre as commercial customers.
Instead of standardizing evaluations around fixed tasks, environments, or locations, we propose to crowd-source evaluations across a distributed network of evaluators.

In this report, we describe our methodology for constructing RoboChallenge, an online evaluation system to test robotic control algorithms, and our survey of recent state-of-the-art VLA models using our initial benchmark Table30.

ManipulationNet delivers reproducible task setups through standardized hardware kits, and enables distributed performance evaluation via a unified software client that delivers real-time task instructions and collects benchmarking results.

We evaluate RL-100 on eight diverse real-robot tasks, from dynamic pushing and agile bowling to pouring, cloth folding, unscrewing, multi-stage juicing, and long-horizon box folding. RL-100 attains 100 percent success across evaluated trials, for a total of 1000 out of 1000 episodes, including up to 250 out of 250 consecutive trials on one task.

On all of the tasks except diverse laundry, the success rate of the final π*0.6 model is in the 90%+ range. This makes it feasible to use in practical settings, such as making espresso drinks at the office or assembling boxes in a factory, as shown in the accompanying videos.

We present Sparsh-X, the first multisensory touch representations across four tactile modalities: image, audio, motion, and pressure. Trained on ~1M contact-rich interactions collected with the Digit 360 sensor, Sparsh-X captures complementary touch signals at diverse temporal and spatial scales.
We introduce TouchWorld, a predictive-and-reactive tactile foundation model for dexterous manipulation.

We train a Vision Language Action (VLA) model on over 20,854 hours of action labeled egocentric human video, more than 20 times larger than prior efforts, and uncover a log linear scaling law between human data scale and validation loss. This validation loss strongly correlates with downstream real robot performance, establishing large scale human data as a predictable supervision source.
